                <div class="main__content main__content--unboxed" itemprop="articleBody">
                    
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Ordinary meetings of Council are held at the Triabunna Council Offices typically on the fourth Tuesday of each month commencing at 2pm. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Meetings are live streamed on <a href="https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCf2HcUP3LbxaCCSqhRi-Nlg">Council’s YouTube channel</a> and members of the public are invited to register to attend the Council Meeting in person.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><a href="https://assets.gsbc.tas.gov.au/uploads/2026/09/Notice-of-Council-Meetings-Glamorgan-Spring-Bay-Council-2026.pdf">Notice of Council Meetings – Glamrogan Spring Bay Council 2026 </a></p>



<div class="wp-block-ionata-accordion-block b-accordion" data-auto-close="true" data-is-animated="true"><details class="b-accordion__container"><summary class="b-accordion-head"><h2 id="at-3670" class="b-accordion-head__title">How do I ask a question?</h2><i class="b-accordion-head__indicator" aria-hidden="true"></i></summary><div class="b-accordion-body"><div id="ac-3670" class="b-accordion-body__inner">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Local government is the only level of government where the public gallery can ask questions in the<br>Chamber. This privilege does bring with it a required level of common courtesy and mutual respect<br>between the public, your elected members and the institution of Municipal Council.</p>



<ol class="wp-block-list">
<li>Glamorgan Spring Bay Council allows a minimum of 15 minutes in total for Public Question Time<br>during Ordinary Meetings of Council.</li>



<li>Questions are to be addressed to the Chairperson.</li>



<li>Questions addressing the personal actions of a Councillor/s may not be accepted by the Chairperson.</li>



<li>Questions must only relate to the activities of Council.</li>



<li>Public statements will not be allowed during Public Question Time. The Council requests that Public Question Time is used for questions only.</li>



<li>A question asked at a meeting is to, as far as is practicable –
<ul class="wp-block-list">
<li>(a) be concise; and</li>



<li>(b) be clear; and</li>



<li>(c) not be a statement; and</li>



<li>(d) have minimal pre-amble.</li>
</ul>
</li>



<li>Prior to the commencement of a Council Meeting, the Chairperson will approach the public gallery and request the names of those who wish to ask a question during Public Question Time.</li>



<li>Council encourages wherever possible, that questions are submitted in writing to the Mayor on the day or to the General Manager 7 days in advance of the meeting date. If the question is submitted 7 days prior, it is considered to be taken ‘on notice’ and a response will be provided in the meeting agenda.</li>



<li>A question may be taken on notice and answered at the next Ordinary Meeting of Council.  </li>



<li>A question by any member of the public and any answer to a question is not to be debated.</li>



<li>The Chair of the meeting can refuse a question but must explain why a question is being refused. Inappropriate questions that are offensive in nature, relate to personnel, confidential or legal matters involving Council or are not Council business will not be accepted.</li>



<li>There is a limit of two (2) questions per person either in writing or in person.</li>
</ol>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Please note: The rules for asking a question during Public Question Time are governed by regulation 36 of the Local Government (Meeting Procedures) 2025 and the Chair of the meeting.</p>
</div></div></details></div>



<div class="wp-block-ionata-accordion-block b-accordion" data-auto-close="true" data-is-animated="true"><details class="b-accordion__container"><summary class="b-accordion-head"><h2 id="at-3671" class="b-accordion-head__title">How do I attend a meeting?</h2><i class="b-accordion-head__indicator" aria-hidden="true"></i></summary><div class="b-accordion-body"><div id="ac-3671" class="b-accordion-body__inner">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Attending a Council Meeting</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Members of the public are welcome to attend Council Meetings in person. The Chambers can accommodate up to nine visitors per meeting, and attendance is by registration only — once we reach capacity, no further registrations can be accepted.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Register to attend — email admin@freycinet.tas.gov.au or call our Executive Officer on (03) 6256 4777.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Public Question Time — if you’d like to ask a question but can’t attend, you can submit it in writing by 12 noon the day before the meeting. Either email admin@freycinet, or drop your question into the post box outside the Council Chambers at 9 Melbourne Street, Triabunna.<br></p>
</div></div></details></div>

                <div class="main__content main__content--unboxed" itemprop="articleBody">
                    
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Ordinary meetings of Council are held at the Triabunna Council Offices typically on the fourth Tuesday of each month commencing at 2pm. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Meetings are live streamed on <a href="https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCf2HcUP3LbxaCCSqhRi-Nlg">Council’s YouTube channel</a> and members of the public are invited to register to attend the Council Meeting in person.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><a href="https://assets.gsbc.tas.gov.au/uploads/2026/09/Notice-of-Council-Meetings-Glamorgan-Spring-Bay-Council-2026.pdf">Notice of Council Meetings – Glamrogan Spring Bay Council 2026 </a></p>



<div class="wp-block-ionata-accordion-block b-accordion" data-auto-close="true" data-is-animated="true"><details class="b-accordion__container"><summary class="b-accordion-head"><h2 id="at-3670" class="b-accordion-head__title">How do I ask a question?</h2><i class="b-accordion-head__indicator" aria-hidden="true"></i></summary><div class="b-accordion-body"><div id="ac-3670" class="b-accordion-body__inner">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Local government is the only level of government where the public gallery can ask questions in the<br>Chamber. This privilege does bring with it a required level of common courtesy and mutual respect<br>between the public, your elected members and the institution of Municipal Council.</p>



<ol class="wp-block-list">
<li>Glamorgan Spring Bay Council allows a minimum of 15 minutes in total for Public Question Time<br>during Ordinary Meetings of Council.</li>



<li>Questions are to be addressed to the Chairperson.</li>



<li>Questions addressing the personal actions of a Councillor/s may not be accepted by the Chairperson.</li>



<li>Questions must only relate to the activities of Council.</li>



<li>Public statements will not be allowed during Public Question Time. The Council requests that Public Question Time is used for questions only.</li>



<li>A question asked at a meeting is to, as far as is practicable –
<ul class="wp-block-list">
<li>(a) be concise; and</li>



<li>(b) be clear; and</li>



<li>(c) not be a statement; and</li>



<li>(d) have minimal pre-amble.</li>
</ul>
</li>



<li>Prior to the commencement of a Council Meeting, the Chairperson will approach the public gallery and request the names of those who wish to ask a question during Public Question Time.</li>



<li>Council encourages wherever possible, that questions are submitted in writing to the Mayor on the day or to the General Manager 7 days in advance of the meeting date. If the question is submitted 7 days prior, it is considered to be taken ‘on notice’ and a response will be provided in the meeting agenda.</li>



<li>A question may be taken on notice and answered at the next Ordinary Meeting of Council.  </li>



<li>A question by any member of the public and any answer to a question is not to be debated.</li>



<li>The Chair of the meeting can refuse a question but must explain why a question is being refused. Inappropriate questions that are offensive in nature, relate to personnel, confidential or legal matters involving Council or are not Council business will not be accepted.</li>



<li>There is a limit of two (2) questions per person either in writing or in person.</li>
</ol>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Please note: The rules for asking a question during Public Question Time are governed by regulation 36 of the Local Government (Meeting Procedures) 2025 and the Chair of the meeting.</p>
</div></div></details></div>



<div class="wp-block-ionata-accordion-block b-accordion" data-auto-close="true" data-is-animated="true"><details class="b-accordion__container"><summary class="b-accordion-head"><h2 id="at-3671" class="b-accordion-head__title">How do I attend a meeting?</h2><i class="b-accordion-head__indicator" aria-hidden="true"></i></summary><div class="b-accordion-body"><div id="ac-3671" class="b-accordion-body__inner">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Attending a Council Meeting</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Members of the public are welcome to attend Council Meetings in person. The Chambers can accommodate up to nine visitors per meeting, and attendance is by registration only — once we reach capacity, no further registrations can be accepted.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Register to attend — email admin@freycinet.tas.gov.au or call our Executive Officer on (03) 6256 4777.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Public Question Time — if you’d like to ask a question but can’t attend, you can submit it in writing by 12 noon the day before the meeting. Either email admin@freycinet, or drop your question into the post box outside the Council Chambers at 9 Melbourne Street, Triabunna.<br></p>
</div></div></details></div>

                <div class="main__content main__content--unboxed" itemprop="articleBody">
                    
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Ordinary meetings of Council are held at the Triabunna Council Offices typically on the fourth Tuesday of each month commencing at 2pm. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Meetings are live streamed on <a href="https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCf2HcUP3LbxaCCSqhRi-Nlg">Council’s YouTube channel</a> and members of the public are invited to register to attend the Council Meeting in person.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><a href="https://assets.gsbc.tas.gov.au/uploads/2026/09/Notice-of-Council-Meetings-Glamorgan-Spring-Bay-Council-2026.pdf">Notice of Council Meetings – Glamrogan Spring Bay Council 2026 </a></p>



<div class="wp-block-ionata-accordion-block b-accordion" data-auto-close="true" data-is-animated="true"><details class="b-accordion__container"><summary class="b-accordion-head"><h2 id="at-3670" class="b-accordion-head__title">How do I ask a question?</h2><i class="b-accordion-head__indicator" aria-hidden="true"></i></summary><div class="b-accordion-body"><div id="ac-3670" class="b-accordion-body__inner">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Local government is the only level of government where the public gallery can ask questions in the<br>Chamber. This privilege does bring with it a required level of common courtesy and mutual respect<br>between the public, your elected members and the institution of Municipal Council.</p>



<ol class="wp-block-list">
<li>Glamorgan Spring Bay Council allows a minimum of 15 minutes in total for Public Question Time<br>during Ordinary Meetings of Council.</li>



<li>Questions are to be addressed to the Chairperson.</li>



<li>Questions addressing the personal actions of a Councillor/s may not be accepted by the Chairperson.</li>



<li>Questions must only relate to the activities of Council.</li>



<li>Public statements will not be allowed during Public Question Time. The Council requests that Public Question Time is used for questions only.</li>



<li>A question asked at a meeting is to, as far as is practicable –
<ul class="wp-block-list">
<li>(a) be concise; and</li>



<li>(b) be clear; and</li>



<li>(c) not be a statement; and</li>



<li>(d) have minimal pre-amble.</li>
</ul>
</li>



<li>Prior to the commencement of a Council Meeting, the Chairperson will approach the public gallery and request the names of those who wish to ask a question during Public Question Time.</li>



<li>Council encourages wherever possible, that questions are submitted in writing to the Mayor on the day or to the General Manager 7 days in advance of the meeting date. If the question is submitted 7 days prior, it is considered to be taken ‘on notice’ and a response will be provided in the meeting agenda.</li>



<li>A question may be taken on notice and answered at the next Ordinary Meeting of Council.  </li>



<li>A question by any member of the public and any answer to a question is not to be debated.</li>



<li>The Chair of the meeting can refuse a question but must explain why a question is being refused. Inappropriate questions that are offensive in nature, relate to personnel, confidential or legal matters involving Council or are not Council business will not be accepted.</li>



<li>There is a limit of two (2) questions per person either in writing or in person.</li>
</ol>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Please note: The rules for asking a question during Public Question Time are governed by regulation 36 of the Local Government (Meeting Procedures) 2025 and the Chair of the meeting.</p>
</div></div></details></div>



<div class="wp-block-ionata-accordion-block b-accordion" data-auto-close="true" data-is-animated="true"><details class="b-accordion__container"><summary class="b-accordion-head"><h2 id="at-3671" class="b-accordion-head__title">How do I attend a meeting?</h2><i class="b-accordion-head__indicator" aria-hidden="true"></i></summary><div class="b-accordion-body"><div id="ac-3671" class="b-accordion-body__inner">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Attending a Council Meeting</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Members of the public are welcome to attend Council Meetings in person. The Chambers can accommodate up to nine visitors per meeting, and attendance is by registration only — once we reach capacity, no further registrations can be accepted.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Register to attend — email admin@freycinet.tas.gov.au or call our Executive Officer on (03) 6256 4777.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Public Question Time — if you’d like to ask a question but can’t attend, you can submit it in writing by 12 noon the day before the meeting. Either email admin@freycinet, or drop your question into the post box outside the Council Chambers at 9 Melbourne Street, Triabunna.<br></p>
</div></div></details></div>



<div class="wp-block-ionata-accordion-block b-accordion" data-auto-close="true" data-is-animated="true"><details class="b-accordion__container"><summary class="b-accordion-head"><h2 id="at-3672" class="b-accordion-head__title">Annual General Meeting procedure</h2><i class="b-accordion-head__indicator" aria-hidden="true"></i></summary><div class="b-accordion-body"><div id="ac-3672" class="b-accordion-body__inner">

</div></div></details></div>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"></p>

                <div class="main__content main__content--unboxed" itemprop="articleBody">
                    
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Ordinary meetings of Council are held at the Triabunna Council Offices typically on the fourth Tuesday of each month commencing at 2pm. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Meetings are live streamed on <a href="https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCf2HcUP3LbxaCCSqhRi-Nlg">Council’s YouTube channel</a> and members of the public are invited to register to attend the Council Meeting in person.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><a href="https://assets.gsbc.tas.gov.au/uploads/2026/09/Notice-of-Council-Meetings-Glamorgan-Spring-Bay-Council-2026.pdf">Notice of Council Meetings – Glamrogan Spring Bay Council 2026 </a></p>



<div class="wp-block-ionata-accordion-block b-accordion" data-auto-close="true" data-is-animated="true"><details class="b-accordion__container"><summary class="b-accordion-head"><h2 id="at-3670" class="b-accordion-head__title">How do I ask a question?</h2><i class="b-accordion-head__indicator" aria-hidden="true"></i></summary><div class="b-accordion-body"><div id="ac-3670" class="b-accordion-body__inner">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Local government is the only level of government where the public gallery can ask questions in the<br>Chamber. This privilege does bring with it a required level of common courtesy and mutual respect<br>between the public, your elected members and the institution of Municipal Council.</p>



<ol class="wp-block-list">
<li>Glamorgan Spring Bay Council allows a minimum of 15 minutes in total for Public Question Time<br>during Ordinary Meetings of Council.</li>



<li>Questions are to be addressed to the Chairperson.</li>



<li>Questions addressing the personal actions of a Councillor/s may not be accepted by the Chairperson.</li>



<li>Questions must only relate to the activities of Council.</li>



<li>Public statements will not be allowed during Public Question Time. The Council requests that Public Question Time is used for questions only.</li>



<li>A question asked at a meeting is to, as far as is practicable –
<ul class="wp-block-list">
<li>(a) be concise; and</li>



<li>(b) be clear; and</li>



<li>(c) not be a statement; and</li>



<li>(d) have minimal pre-amble.</li>
</ul>
</li>



<li>Prior to the commencement of a Council Meeting, the Chairperson will approach the public gallery and request the names of those who wish to ask a question during Public Question Time.</li>



<li>Council encourages wherever possible, that questions are submitted in writing to the Mayor on the day or to the General Manager 7 days in advance of the meeting date. If the question is submitted 7 days prior, it is considered to be taken ‘on notice’ and a response will be provided in the meeting agenda.</li>



<li>A question may be taken on notice and answered at the next Ordinary Meeting of Council.  </li>



<li>A question by any member of the public and any answer to a question is not to be debated.</li>



<li>The Chair of the meeting can refuse a question but must explain why a question is being refused. Inappropriate questions that are offensive in nature, relate to personnel, confidential or legal matters involving Council or are not Council business will not be accepted.</li>



<li>There is a limit of two (2) questions per person either in writing or in person.</li>
</ol>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Please note: The rules for asking a question during Public Question Time are governed by regulation 36 of the Local Government (Meeting Procedures) 2025 and the Chair of the meeting.</p>
</div></div></details></div>



<div class="wp-block-ionata-accordion-block b-accordion" data-auto-close="true" data-is-animated="true"><details class="b-accordion__container"><summary class="b-accordion-head"><h2 id="at-3671" class="b-accordion-head__title">How do I attend a meeting?</h2><i class="b-accordion-head__indicator" aria-hidden="true"></i></summary><div class="b-accordion-body"><div id="ac-3671" class="b-accordion-body__inner">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Attending a Council Meeting</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Members of the public are welcome to attend Council Meetings in person. The Chambers can accommodate up to nine visitors per meeting, and attendance is by registration only — once we reach capacity, no further registrations can be accepted.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Register to attend — email admin@freycinet.tas.gov.au or call our Executive Officer on (03) 6256 4777.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Public Question Time — if you’d like to ask a question but can’t attend, you can submit it in writing by 12 noon the day before the meeting. Either email admin@freycinet, or drop your question into the post box outside the Council Chambers at 9 Melbourne Street, Triabunna.<br></p>
</div></div></details></div>

</div></div></details></div>

<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Ordinary meetings of Council are held at the Triabunna Council Offices typically on the fourth Tuesday of each month commencing at 2pm. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Meetings are live streamed on <a href="https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCf2HcUP3LbxaCCSqhRi-Nlg">Council’s YouTube channel</a> and members of the public are invited to register to attend the Council Meeting in person.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><a href="https://assets.gsbc.tas.gov.au/uploads/2026/09/Notice-of-Council-Meetings-Glamorgan-Spring-Bay-Council-2026.pdf">Notice of Council Meetings – Glamrogan Spring Bay Council 2026 </a></p>



<div class="wp-block-ionata-accordion-block b-accordion" data-auto-close="true" data-is-animated="true"><details class="b-accordion__container"><summary class="b-accordion-head"><h2 id="at-3670" class="b-accordion-head__title">How do I ask a question?</h2><i class="b-accordion-head__indicator" aria-hidden="true"></i></summary><div class="b-accordion-body"><div id="ac-3670" class="b-accordion-body__inner">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Local government is the only level of government where the public gallery can ask questions in the<br>Chamber. This privilege does bring with it a required level of common courtesy and mutual respect<br>between the public, your elected members and the institution of Municipal Council.</p>



<ol class="wp-block-list">
<li>Glamorgan Spring Bay Council allows a minimum of 15 minutes in total for Public Question Time<br>during Ordinary Meetings of Council.</li>



<li>Questions are to be addressed to the Chairperson.</li>



<li>Questions addressing the personal actions of a Councillor/s may not be accepted by the Chairperson.</li>



<li>Questions must only relate to the activities of Council.</li>



<li>Public statements will not be allowed during Public Question Time. The Council requests that Public Question Time is used for questions only.</li>



<li>A question asked at a meeting is to, as far as is practicable –
<ul class="wp-block-list">
<li>(a) be concise; and</li>



<li>(b) be clear; and</li>



<li>(c) not be a statement; and</li>



<li>(d) have minimal pre-amble.</li>
</ul>
</li>



<li>Prior to the commencement of a Council Meeting, the Chairperson will approach the public gallery and request the names of those who wish to ask a question during Public Question Time.</li>



<li>Council encourages wherever possible, that questions are submitted in writing to the Mayor on the day or to the General Manager 7 days in advance of the meeting date. If the question is submitted 7 days prior, it is considered to be taken ‘on notice’ and a response will be provided in the meeting agenda.</li>



<li>A question may be taken on notice and answered at the next Ordinary Meeting of Council.  </li>



<li>A question by any member of the public and any answer to a question is not to be debated.</li>



<li>The Chair of the meeting can refuse a question but must explain why a question is being refused. Inappropriate questions that are offensive in nature, relate to personnel, confidential or legal matters involving Council or are not Council business will not be accepted.</li>



<li>There is a limit of two (2) questions per person either in writing or in person.</li>
</ol>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Please note: The rules for asking a question during Public Question Time are governed by regulation 36 of the Local Government (Meeting Procedures) 2025 and the Chair of the meeting.</p>
</div></div></details></div>



<div class="wp-block-ionata-accordion-block b-accordion" data-auto-close="true" data-is-animated="true"><details class="b-accordion__container"><summary class="b-accordion-head"><h2 id="at-3671" class="b-accordion-head__title">How do I attend a meeting?</h2><i class="b-accordion-head__indicator" aria-hidden="true"></i></summary><div class="b-accordion-body"><div id="ac-3671" class="b-accordion-body__inner">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Attending a Council Meeting</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Members of the public are welcome to attend Council Meetings in person. The Chambers can accommodate up to nine visitors per meeting, and attendance is by registration only — once we reach capacity, no further registrations can be accepted.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Register to attend — email admin@freycinet.tas.gov.au or call our Executive Officer on (03) 6256 4777.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Public Question Time — if you’d like to ask a question but can’t attend, you can submit it in writing by 12 noon the day before the meeting. Either email admin@freycinet, or drop your question into the post box outside the Council Chambers at 9 Melbourne Street, Triabunna.<br></p>
</div></div></details></div>

                <div class="main__content main__content--unboxed" itemprop="articleBody">
                    
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Ordinary meetings of Council are held at the Triabunna Council Offices typically on the fourth Tuesday of each month commencing at 2pm. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Meetings are live streamed on <a href="https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCf2HcUP3LbxaCCSqhRi-Nlg">Council’s YouTube channel</a> and members of the public are invited to register to attend the Council Meeting in person.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><a href="https://assets.gsbc.tas.gov.au/uploads/2026/09/Notice-of-Council-Meetings-Glamorgan-Spring-Bay-Council-2026.pdf">Notice of Council Meetings – Glamrogan Spring Bay Council 2026 </a></p>



<div class="wp-block-ionata-accordion-block b-accordion" data-auto-close="true" data-is-animated="true"><details class="b-accordion__container"><summary class="b-accordion-head"><h2 id="at-3670" class="b-accordion-head__title">How do I ask a question?</h2><i class="b-accordion-head__indicator" aria-hidden="true"></i></summary><div class="b-accordion-body"><div id="ac-3670" class="b-accordion-body__inner">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Local government is the only level of government where the public gallery can ask questions in the<br>Chamber. This privilege does bring with it a required level of common courtesy and mutual respect<br>between the public, your elected members and the institution of Municipal Council.</p>



<ol class="wp-block-list">
<li>Glamorgan Spring Bay Council allows a minimum of 15 minutes in total for Public Question Time<br>during Ordinary Meetings of Council.</li>



<li>Questions are to be addressed to the Chairperson.</li>



<li>Questions addressing the personal actions of a Councillor/s may not be accepted by the Chairperson.</li>



<li>Questions must only relate to the activities of Council.</li>



<li>Public statements will not be allowed during Public Question Time. The Council requests that Public Question Time is used for questions only.</li>



<li>A question asked at a meeting is to, as far as is practicable –
<ul class="wp-block-list">
<li>(a) be concise; and</li>



<li>(b) be clear; and</li>



<li>(c) not be a statement; and</li>



<li>(d) have minimal pre-amble.</li>
</ul>
</li>



<li>Prior to the commencement of a Council Meeting, the Chairperson will approach the public gallery and request the names of those who wish to ask a question during Public Question Time.</li>



<li>Council encourages wherever possible, that questions are submitted in writing to the Mayor on the day or to the General Manager 7 days in advance of the meeting date. If the question is submitted 7 days prior, it is considered to be taken ‘on notice’ and a response will be provided in the meeting agenda.</li>



<li>A question may be taken on notice and answered at the next Ordinary Meeting of Council.  </li>



<li>A question by any member of the public and any answer to a question is not to be debated.</li>



<li>The Chair of the meeting can refuse a question but must explain why a question is being refused. Inappropriate questions that are offensive in nature, relate to personnel, confidential or legal matters involving Council or are not Council business will not be accepted.</li>



<li>There is a limit of two (2) questions per person either in writing or in person.</li>
</ol>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Please note: The rules for asking a question during Public Question Time are governed by regulation 36 of the Local Government (Meeting Procedures) 2025 and the Chair of the meeting.</p>
</div></div></details></div>



<div class="wp-block-ionata-accordion-block b-accordion" data-auto-close="true" data-is-animated="true"><details class="b-accordion__container"><summary class="b-accordion-head"><h2 id="at-3671" class="b-accordion-head__title">How do I attend a meeting?</h2><i class="b-accordion-head__indicator" aria-hidden="true"></i></summary><div class="b-accordion-body"><div id="ac-3671" class="b-accordion-body__inner">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Attending a Council Meeting</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Members of the public are welcome to attend Council Meetings in person. The Chambers can accommodate up to nine visitors per meeting, and attendance is by registration only — once we reach capacity, no further registrations can be accepted.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Register to attend — email admin@freycinet.tas.gov.au or call our Executive Officer on (03) 6256 4777.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Public Question Time — if you’d like to ask a question but can’t attend, you can submit it in writing by 12 noon the day before the meeting. Either email admin@freycinet, or drop your question into the post box outside the Council Chambers at 9 Melbourne Street, Triabunna.<br></p>
</div></div></details></div>

                <div class="main__content main__content--unboxed" itemprop="articleBody">
                    
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Ordinary meetings of Council are held at the Triabunna Council Offices typically on the fourth Tuesday of each month commencing at 2pm. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Meetings are live streamed on <a href="https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCf2HcUP3LbxaCCSqhRi-Nlg">Council’s YouTube channel</a> and members of the public are invited to register to attend the Council Meeting in person.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><a href="https://assets.gsbc.tas.gov.au/uploads/2026/09/Notice-of-Council-Meetings-Glamorgan-Spring-Bay-Council-2026.pdf">Notice of Council Meetings – Glamrogan Spring Bay Council 2026 </a></p>



<div class="wp-block-ionata-accordion-block b-accordion" data-auto-close="true" data-is-animated="true"><details class="b-accordion__container"><summary class="b-accordion-head"><h2 id="at-3670" class="b-accordion-head__title">How do I ask a question?</h2><i class="b-accordion-head__indicator" aria-hidden="true"></i></summary><div class="b-accordion-body"><div id="ac-3670" class="b-accordion-body__inner">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Local government is the only level of government where the public gallery can ask questions in the<br>Chamber. This privilege does bring with it a required level of common courtesy and mutual respect<br>between the public, your elected members and the institution of Municipal Council.</p>



<ol class="wp-block-list">
<li>Glamorgan Spring Bay Council allows a minimum of 15 minutes in total for Public Question Time<br>during Ordinary Meetings of Council.</li>



<li>Questions are to be addressed to the Chairperson.</li>



<li>Questions addressing the personal actions of a Councillor/s may not be accepted by the Chairperson.</li>



<li>Questions must only relate to the activities of Council.</li>



<li>Public statements will not be allowed during Public Question Time. The Council requests that Public Question Time is used for questions only.</li>



<li>A question asked at a meeting is to, as far as is practicable –
<ul class="wp-block-list">
<li>(a) be concise; and</li>



<li>(b) be clear; and</li>



<li>(c) not be a statement; and</li>



<li>(d) have minimal pre-amble.</li>
</ul>
</li>



<li>Prior to the commencement of a Council Meeting, the Chairperson will approach the public gallery and request the names of those who wish to ask a question during Public Question Time.</li>



<li>Council encourages wherever possible, that questions are submitted in writing to the Mayor on the day or to the General Manager 7 days in advance of the meeting date. If the question is submitted 7 days prior, it is considered to be taken ‘on notice’ and a response will be provided in the meeting agenda.</li>



<li>A question may be taken on notice and answered at the next Ordinary Meeting of Council.  </li>



<li>A question by any member of the public and any answer to a question is not to be debated.</li>



<li>The Chair of the meeting can refuse a question but must explain why a question is being refused. Inappropriate questions that are offensive in nature, relate to personnel, confidential or legal matters involving Council or are not Council business will not be accepted.</li>



<li>There is a limit of two (2) questions per person either in writing or in person.</li>
</ol>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Please note: The rules for asking a question during Public Question Time are governed by regulation 36 of the Local Government (Meeting Procedures) 2025 and the Chair of the meeting.</p>
</div></div></details></div>



<div class="wp-block-ionata-accordion-block b-accordion" data-auto-close="true" data-is-animated="true"><details class="b-accordion__container"><summary class="b-accordion-head"><h2 id="at-3671" class="b-accordion-head__title">How do I attend a meeting?</h2><i class="b-accordion-head__indicator" aria-hidden="true"></i></summary><div class="b-accordion-body"><div id="ac-3671" class="b-accordion-body__inner">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Attending a Council Meeting</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Members of the public are welcome to attend Council Meetings in person. The Chambers can accommodate up to nine visitors per meeting, and attendance is by registration only — once we reach capacity, no further registrations can be accepted.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Register to attend — email admin@freycinet.tas.gov.au or call our Executive Officer on (03) 6256 4777.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Public Question Time — if you’d like to ask a question but can’t attend, you can submit it in writing by 12 noon the day before the meeting. Either email admin@freycinet, or drop your question into the post box outside the Council Chambers at 9 Melbourne Street, Triabunna.<br></p>
</div></div></details></div>

                <div class="main__content main__content--unboxed" itemprop="articleBody">
                    
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Ordinary meetings of Council are held at the Triabunna Council Offices typically on the fourth Tuesday of each month commencing at 2pm. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Meetings are live streamed on <a href="https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCf2HcUP3LbxaCCSqhRi-Nlg">Council’s YouTube channel</a> and members of the public are invited to register to attend the Council Meeting in person.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><a href="https://assets.gsbc.tas.gov.au/uploads/2026/09/Notice-of-Council-Meetings-Glamorgan-Spring-Bay-Council-2026.pdf">Notice of Council Meetings – Glamrogan Spring Bay Council 2026 </a></p>



<div class="wp-block-ionata-accordion-block b-accordion" data-auto-close="true" data-is-animated="true"><details class="b-accordion__container"><summary class="b-accordion-head"><h2 id="at-3670" class="b-accordion-head__title">How do I ask a question?</h2><i class="b-accordion-head__indicator" aria-hidden="true"></i></summary><div class="b-accordion-body"><div id="ac-3670" class="b-accordion-body__inner">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Local government is the only level of government where the public gallery can ask questions in the<br>Chamber. This privilege does bring with it a required level of common courtesy and mutual respect<br>between the public, your elected members and the institution of Municipal Council.</p>



<ol class="wp-block-list">
<li>Glamorgan Spring Bay Council allows a minimum of 15 minutes in total for Public Question Time<br>during Ordinary Meetings of Council.</li>



<li>Questions are to be addressed to the Chairperson.</li>



<li>Questions addressing the personal actions of a Councillor/s may not be accepted by the Chairperson.</li>



<li>Questions must only relate to the activities of Council.</li>



<li>Public statements will not be allowed during Public Question Time. The Council requests that Public Question Time is used for questions only.</li>



<li>A question asked at a meeting is to, as far as is practicable –
<ul class="wp-block-list">
<li>(a) be concise; and</li>



<li>(b) be clear; and</li>



<li>(c) not be a statement; and</li>



<li>(d) have minimal pre-amble.</li>
</ul>
</li>



<li>Prior to the commencement of a Council Meeting, the Chairperson will approach the public gallery and request the names of those who wish to ask a question during Public Question Time.</li>



<li>Council encourages wherever possible, that questions are submitted in writing to the Mayor on the day or to the General Manager 7 days in advance of the meeting date. If the question is submitted 7 days prior, it is considered to be taken ‘on notice’ and a response will be provided in the meeting agenda.</li>



<li>A question may be taken on notice and answered at the next Ordinary Meeting of Council.  </li>



<li>A question by any member of the public and any answer to a question is not to be debated.</li>



<li>The Chair of the meeting can refuse a question but must explain why a question is being refused. Inappropriate questions that are offensive in nature, relate to personnel, confidential or legal matters involving Council or are not Council business will not be accepted.</li>



<li>There is a limit of two (2) questions per person either in writing or in person.</li>
</ol>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Please note: The rules for asking a question during Public Question Time are governed by regulation 36 of the Local Government (Meeting Procedures) 2025 and the Chair of the meeting.</p>
</div></div></details></div>



<div class="wp-block-ionata-accordion-block b-accordion" data-auto-close="true" data-is-animated="true"><details class="b-accordion__container"><summary class="b-accordion-head"><h2 id="at-3671" class="b-accordion-head__title">How do I attend a meeting?</h2><i class="b-accordion-head__indicator" aria-hidden="true"></i></summary><div class="b-accordion-body"><div id="ac-3671" class="b-accordion-body__inner">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Attending a Council Meeting</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Members of the public are welcome to attend Council Meetings in person. The Chambers can accommodate up to nine visitors per meeting, and attendance is by registration only — once we reach capacity, no further registrations can be accepted.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Register to attend — email admin@freycinet.tas.gov.au or call our Executive Officer on (03) 6256 4777.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Public Question Time — if you’d like to ask a question but can’t attend, you can submit it in writing by 12 noon the day before the meeting. Either email admin@freycinet, or drop your question into the post box outside the Council Chambers at 9 Melbourne Street, Triabunna.<br></p>
</div></div></details></div>



<div class="wp-block-ionata-accordion-block b-accordion" data-auto-close="true" data-is-animated="true"><details class="b-accordion__container"><summary class="b-accordion-head"><h2 id="at-3672" class="b-accordion-head__title">Annual General Meeting procedure</h2><i class="b-accordion-head__indicator" aria-hidden="true"></i></summary><div class="b-accordion-body"><div id="ac-3672" class="b-accordion-body__inner">

</div></div></details></div>

                <div class="main__content main__content--unboxed" itemprop="articleBody">
                    
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Ordinary meetings of Council are held at the Triabunna Council Offices typically on the fourth Tuesday of each month commencing at 2pm. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Meetings are live streamed on <a href="https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCf2HcUP3LbxaCCSqhRi-Nlg">Council’s YouTube channel</a> and members of the public are invited to register to attend the Council Meeting in person.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><a href="https://assets.gsbc.tas.gov.au/uploads/2026/09/Notice-of-Council-Meetings-Glamorgan-Spring-Bay-Council-2026.pdf">Notice of Council Meetings – Glamrogan Spring Bay Council 2026 </a></p>



<div class="wp-block-ionata-accordion-block b-accordion" data-auto-close="true" data-is-animated="true"><details class="b-accordion__container"><summary class="b-accordion-head"><h2 id="at-3670" class="b-accordion-head__title">How do I ask a question?</h2><i class="b-accordion-head__indicator" aria-hidden="true"></i></summary><div class="b-accordion-body"><div id="ac-3670" class="b-accordion-body__inner">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Local government is the only level of government where the public gallery can ask questions in the<br>Chamber. This privilege does bring with it a required level of common courtesy and mutual respect<br>between the public, your elected members and the institution of Municipal Council.</p>



<ol class="wp-block-list">
<li>Glamorgan Spring Bay Council allows a minimum of 15 minutes in total for Public Question Time<br>during Ordinary Meetings of Council.</li>



<li>Questions are to be addressed to the Chairperson.</li>



<li>Questions addressing the personal actions of a Councillor/s may not be accepted by the Chairperson.</li>



<li>Questions must only relate to the activities of Council.</li>



<li>Public statements will not be allowed during Public Question Time. The Council requests that Public Question Time is used for questions only.</li>



<li>A question asked at a meeting is to, as far as is practicable –
<ul class="wp-block-list">
<li>(a) be concise; and</li>



<li>(b) be clear; and</li>



<li>(c) not be a statement; and</li>



<li>(d) have minimal pre-amble.</li>
</ul>
</li>



<li>Prior to the commencement of a Council Meeting, the Chairperson will approach the public gallery and request the names of those who wish to ask a question during Public Question Time.</li>



<li>Council encourages wherever possible, that questions are submitted in writing to the Mayor on the day or to the General Manager 7 days in advance of the meeting date. If the question is submitted 7 days prior, it is considered to be taken ‘on notice’ and a response will be provided in the meeting agenda.</li>



<li>A question may be taken on notice and answered at the next Ordinary Meeting of Council.  </li>



<li>A question by any member of the public and any answer to a question is not to be debated.</li>



<li>The Chair of the meeting can refuse a question but must explain why a question is being refused. Inappropriate questions that are offensive in nature, relate to personnel, confidential or legal matters involving Council or are not Council business will not be accepted.</li>



<li>There is a limit of two (2) questions per person either in writing or in person.</li>
</ol>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Please note: The rules for asking a question during Public Question Time are governed by regulation 36 of the Local Government (Meeting Procedures) 2025 and the Chair of the meeting.</p>
</div></div></details></div>



<div class="wp-block-ionata-accordion-block b-accordion" data-auto-close="true" data-is-animated="true"><details class="b-accordion__container"><summary class="b-accordion-head"><h2 id="at-3671" class="b-accordion-head__title">How do I attend a meeting?</h2><i class="b-accordion-head__indicator" aria-hidden="true"></i></summary><div class="b-accordion-body"><div id="ac-3671" class="b-accordion-body__inner">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Attending a Council Meeting</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Members of the public are welcome to attend Council Meetings in person. The Chambers can accommodate up to nine visitors per meeting, and attendance is by registration only — once we reach capacity, no further registrations can be accepted.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Register to attend — email admin@freycinet.tas.gov.au or call our Executive Officer on (03) 6256 4777.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Public Question Time — if you’d like to ask a question but can’t attend, you can submit it in writing by 12 noon the day before the meeting. Either email admin@freycinet, or drop your question into the post box outside the Council Chambers at 9 Melbourne Street, Triabunna.<br></p>
</div></div></details></div>

</div></div></details></div>

<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Ordinary meetings of Council are held at the Triabunna Council Offices typically on the fourth Tuesday of each month commencing at 2pm. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Meetings are live streamed on <a href="https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCf2HcUP3LbxaCCSqhRi-Nlg">Council’s YouTube channel</a> and members of the public are invited to register to attend the Council Meeting in person.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><a href="https://assets.gsbc.tas.gov.au/uploads/2026/09/Notice-of-Council-Meetings-Glamorgan-Spring-Bay-Council-2026.pdf">Notice of Council Meetings – Glamrogan Spring Bay Council 2026 </a></p>



<div class="wp-block-ionata-accordion-block b-accordion" data-auto-close="true" data-is-animated="true"><details class="b-accordion__container"><summary class="b-accordion-head"><h2 id="at-3670" class="b-accordion-head__title">How do I ask a question?</h2><i class="b-accordion-head__indicator" aria-hidden="true"></i></summary><div class="b-accordion-body"><div id="ac-3670" class="b-accordion-body__inner">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Local government is the only level of government where the public gallery can ask questions in the<br>Chamber. This privilege does bring with it a required level of common courtesy and mutual respect<br>between the public, your elected members and the institution of Municipal Council.</p>



<ol class="wp-block-list">
<li>Glamorgan Spring Bay Council allows a minimum of 15 minutes in total for Public Question Time<br>during Ordinary Meetings of Council.</li>



<li>Questions are to be addressed to the Chairperson.</li>



<li>Questions addressing the personal actions of a Councillor/s may not be accepted by the Chairperson.</li>



<li>Questions must only relate to the activities of Council.</li>



<li>Public statements will not be allowed during Public Question Time. The Council requests that Public Question Time is used for questions only.</li>



<li>A question asked at a meeting is to, as far as is practicable –
<ul class="wp-block-list">
<li>(a) be concise; and</li>



<li>(b) be clear; and</li>



<li>(c) not be a statement; and</li>



<li>(d) have minimal pre-amble.</li>
</ul>
</li>



<li>Prior to the commencement of a Council Meeting, the Chairperson will approach the public gallery and request the names of those who wish to ask a question during Public Question Time.</li>



<li>Council encourages wherever possible, that questions are submitted in writing to the Mayor on the day or to the General Manager 7 days in advance of the meeting date. If the question is submitted 7 days prior, it is considered to be taken ‘on notice’ and a response will be provided in the meeting agenda.</li>



<li>A question may be taken on notice and answered at the next Ordinary Meeting of Council.  </li>



<li>A question by any member of the public and any answer to a question is not to be debated.</li>



<li>The Chair of the meeting can refuse a question but must explain why a question is being refused. Inappropriate questions that are offensive in nature, relate to personnel, confidential or legal matters involving Council or are not Council business will not be accepted.</li>



<li>There is a limit of two (2) questions per person either in writing or in person.</li>
</ol>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Please note: The rules for asking a question during Public Question Time are governed by regulation 36 of the Local Government (Meeting Procedures) 2025 and the Chair of the meeting.</p>
</div></div></details></div>



<div class="wp-block-ionata-accordion-block b-accordion" data-auto-close="true" data-is-animated="true"><details class="b-accordion__container"><summary class="b-accordion-head"><h2 id="at-3671" class="b-accordion-head__title">How do I attend a meeting?</h2><i class="b-accordion-head__indicator" aria-hidden="true"></i></summary><div class="b-accordion-body"><div id="ac-3671" class="b-accordion-body__inner">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Attending a Council Meeting</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Members of the public are welcome to attend Council Meetings in person. The Chambers can accommodate up to nine visitors per meeting, and attendance is by registration only — once we reach capacity, no further registrations can be accepted.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Register to attend — email admin@freycinet.tas.gov.au or call our Executive Officer on (03) 6256 4777.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Public Question Time — if you’d like to ask a question but can’t attend, you can submit it in writing by 12 noon the day before the meeting. Either email admin@freycinet, or drop your question into the post box outside the Council Chambers at 9 Melbourne Street, Triabunna.<br></p>
</div></div></details></div>
